methodology.scheduling: Controlled commit benchmark: one synchronous logical transaction, one microtask checkpoint, then the same React flushSync checkpoint for every library; timing includes notification delivery and DOM commits, excludes correctness checks. No frame or paint wait.
limitations: Single machine, single browser process, sequential warmed runs; timings are not cross-device performance guarantees.
Headless browser commit latency excludes paint, layout measurement, network, real API libraries and user-event dispatch.
Large arrays use a bounded visible window; this is not a virtualization-library benchmark.
Zustand uses one structurally shared immutable publication per transaction; proxy libraries mutate in place. Representation costs are included.
Results are scenario-specific. Do not combine different workloads into an overall winner.
Fresh stores and roots for every sample; setup and teardown are measured separately. No forced garbage collection; allocation and GC can affect outliers.
Heap retention and memory usage are not measured; allocation work contributes to elapsed times.
Map-and-replace reads and transforms the existing reactive rows; it is not assignment of an already-created plain API response.
